answer_1.quote: We evaluate English text generated by recently-proposed LVLMs on both open-ended and close-form text prompts... Text prompts include "Describe the image in as much detail as possible" and "What are 5 keywords that describe the characteristics of this person?"
answer_1.outputs: Free-form text generations (descriptions, stories, keyword lists, numeric ratings)

answer_2.quote: we utilize Perspective () to evaluate the toxicity of text generated by LVLMs... we define MaxToxicity... we also conduct lexical analyses using Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) and assess competency‑related words.

answer_3.quote: we apply a final filtering step using GPT-4o to determine which words in the PMI lists could be interpreted as reinforcing stereotypes about the target group... we presented the lists of words to GPT-4 (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09) and used the LLM to identify stereotypical words.
methods: filtering PMI lists with a stereotype‑identification prompt

answer_4.quote: three of the authors of this work annotated a subset of generations to verify the correctness of automated toxicity classification... Fleiss' Kappa score for the three human annotations... We also conducted a small manual annotation study where each word was annotated by 3 annotators as being stereotypical/offensive.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators labeled each generated text as either non‑toxic/offensive or potentially toxic/offensive; annotators also labeled words as stereotypical/offensive or not.
